title: Build a Kafka-lite Partitioned Log
summary:
Build the core of Kafka in memory: **topics with N partitions**, key-hash partitioning (FNV-1a), append-only offsets that are never reused, **consumer groups** with deterministic partition assignment and a **rebalance** on every join and leave, **committed offsets** with zombie fencing, consumer lag, and **retention by count**.

The point of the project is the delivery guarantee. Positions reset to the committed offset on rebalance, so anything processed but not committed is **redelivered**. That is at-least-once, and it is why consumers must be idempotent. You will be able to explain per-key ordering, why more consumers than partitions leaves some idle, and what happens when a slow consumer falls behind retention.

milestones.name: M1: Partitions and offsets
milestones.description: FNV-1a hashing, topics with N partitions, per-partition offsets from 0, bounded `read` that returns copies with injected timestamps.

milestones.name: M2: Key partitioning
milestones.description: Same key → same partition, so per-key order is preserved. Null keys round-robin. Keys spread evenly.

milestones.name: M3: Consumer groups and assignment
milestones.description: `joinGroup` / `poll` with fetch positions; round-robin assignment over sorted member ids; generation numbers; idle members when there are more members than partitions.

milestones.name: M4: Commits and lag
milestones.description: Commit the *next* offset to read; only the owner may commit; commits are all-or-nothing; lag = end − committed.

milestones.name: M5: Rebalance and at-least-once
milestones.description: Positions reset to committed on rebalance, so uncommitted records are redelivered to the new owner. Zombies that lost a partition are fenced. Groups are independent.

milestones.name: M6: Retention and multi-topic groups
milestones.description: Retention by count advances the log start without renumbering; consumers behind retention reset to log start; members only get the topics they subscribed to.
